blocks.text: Polygenic inheritance and epistasis are further examples of deviation from Mendel's pattern of inheritance. Both involve more than one gene, but they work differently.

blocks.title: For information: polygenes and epistasis compared
blocks.text: In polygenic inheritance many genes act together, each with a small effect, to produce a trait, which gives continuous variation. In epistasis one allele masks or modifies the effect of another gene, which usually gives discontinuous variation (distinct categories of a trait).

blocks.prompt: Which of the two usually gives continuous variation?
blocks.explanation: Polygenic inheritance; epistasis usually gives distinct categories.

items: Polygenes: many genes add up, continuous variation.
Epistasis: one gene masks another, distinct classes.
